content.text:
I fixed the bug in `canonicalize` in `src/diff/json.ts`. It checked for arrays before it called `toJSON()`, so both cases in the report went wrong. An array's own `toJSON()` was skipped, and a `toJSON()` result that was an array fell into the plain-object branch and came out with numeric keys.

I moved the `toJSON()` call ahead of the array check. The array-versus-object decision is now made on the value `toJSON()` returns, as `JSON.stringify` does. The full suite passes (310 tests), but I didn't add a test for these two cases.

I left the order of the replacer and `toJSON()` as it was: the replacer runs first. `JSON.stringify` does it the other way round, so a custom replacer that inspects values could still see different input than it would there.

I fixed the bug in `canonicalize` in `src/diff/json.ts`. It checked for arrays before it called `toJSON()`, so both cases in the report went wrong. An array's own `toJSON()` was skipped, and a `toJSON()` result that was an array fell into the plain-object branch and came out with numeric keys.

I moved the `toJSON()` call ahead of the array check. The array-versus-object decision is now made on the value `toJSON()` returns, as `JSON.stringify` does. The full suite passes (310 tests), but I didn't add a test for these two cases.

I left the order of the replacer and `toJSON()` as it was: the replacer runs first. `JSON.stringify` does it the other way round, so a custom replacer that inspects values could still see different input than it would there.
